cse-1999-a-23.approach: Newton–Raphson is only locally convergent: it needs a good starting point and a well-behaved derivative, so none of the stated conditions guarantees convergence.

steps.title: Iteration
steps.body: $x_{n+1} = x_n - \dfrac{f(x_n)}{f'(x_n)}$. Convergence (quadratic) is guaranteed only when $x_0$ is close enough to a simple root and $f'$ does not vanish nearby.

steps.title: Counter-examples
steps.body:
- $f(x)=x^3-2x+2$ (a polynomial) with $x_0=0$: $f(0)=2$, $f'(0)=-2$, so $x_1 = 0-\frac{2}{-2}=1$; $f(1)=1$, $f'(1)=1$, so $x_2 = 1-\frac{1}{1}=0$ — it cycles $0,1,0,1,\dots$ forever.
- $f(x)=x^{1/3}$: $x_{n+1}=x_n-\frac{x_n^{1/3}}{\frac13 x_n^{-2/3}}=x_n-3x_n=-2x_n$, which diverges from every $x_0\ne 0$.

So it does not always converge, being a polynomial is not enough, and the sign of $f(x_0)$ is irrelevant.

optionAnalysis.reason: It can cycle or diverge (e.g. $x^{1/3}$, or $x^3-2x+2$ from $x_0=0$).
$x^3-2x+2$ is a polynomial and still cycles between 0 and 1.
The sign of $f(x_0)$ has nothing to do with convergence; replacing $f$ by $-f$ gives the same iterates.
Convergence is only local, so none of the given conditions is sufficient.

cse-1999-a-35.approach: A multi-user, multiprogramming OS must protect processes and itself from user programs: that needs a privileged (kernel) mode and hardware memory protection through address translation/relocation. DMA and demand paging are only performance features.

steps.title: Not needed

- DMA: the CPU can do programmed I/O, just slower.
- Demand paging: many multi-user systems ran with swapping or plain segmentation.
